claim_one_line: L132 SCOUTED BEFORE COMPUTING (the seal-provenance gate's design-time prior-art grep, run at literature scale). VERDICT: the cell as posed would have produced a VACUOUS check and a TEXTBOOK result; scouting cost one panel, computing first would have cost a day and banked a rediscovery. (1) THE ANOMALY CHECK IS PROBABLY VACUOUS: E6 has no symmetrised third-order Casimir and is anomaly-free as a gauge group (Okubo 1977 names it), and on a complete 27 the panel computed 13 U(1) cubic/mixed/gravitational conditions plus [SU(3)]^2 U(1) and [SU(2)]^2 U(1) for all three u(1)s plus the Witten parity (6 doublets, even) -- EVERY ONE VANISHES IDENTICALLY. So if the object's charges form complete 27s the check CANNOT FAIL, and per the programme's own MB12 vacuity rule establishing NON-VACUITY is the prerequisite, not the result: does the spectrum form complete 27s? If not, anomaly cancellation becomes a real constraint and is informative. (2) THE TARGET ALGEBRA IS CLASSIFIED STRUCTURE, RE-DERIVED ON THIS BENCH RATHER THAN ACCEPTED: su(3)+su(2)+u(1)^3 is exactly the A2+A1 LEVI SUBALGEBRA of e6 -- a Levi from node subset S is h + (roots in span S), A2+A1 has 6+2 = 8 roots, so dim = rank + roots = 6+8 = 14, semisimple part = 11, centre = rank - |S| = 6-3 = 3, WHICH ARE EXACTLY B892's THREE NUMBERS. Borel-de Siebenthal 1949 / Dynkin 1952. So ARRIVING at su(3)+su(2)+u(1)^3 from E6 IS NOT A DISCOVERY -- this deflates B892's headline a second time (B950 corrected 'the Standard Model algebra', which is dim 14 not 12; this arc adds that the endpoint is a Levi catalogued 77 years ago). What survives of B892 is THE ROUTE, NOT THE DESTINATION: that the object's own superselection charges pick out THIS Levi; whether that route is novel is a separate question from whether the endpoint is. (3) THE CENTRALIZER ARGUMENT FOR Y DOES NOT TRANSPLANT: the centralizer of su(3)+su(2) is 1-DIMENSIONAL in su(5) -- which IS the Georgi-Glashow textbook definition of hypercharge -- but 9-DIMENSIONAL in e6 (su(3)+u(1)), so 'the u(1) commuting with colour and isospin' does NOT single out Y in E6; an extra input is required and in the literature it is ALWAYS the choice of the SU(5)/SO(10) subgroup, and THAT CHOICE IS THE IDENTIFICATION. (4) Q1's FORCING IS MUCH WEAKER THAN THE FOLKLORE: Minahan-Ramond-Warner get TWO hypercharge solutions from anomalies alone; Babu-Mohapatra get quantisation only if nu is MAJORANA; Foot-Lew-Volkas show charge DE-QUANTISES in the three-generation SM with massless neutrinos, so the forcing is a ONE-GENERATION statement; Lohitsiri-Tong recast it as x^3+y^3=z^3 but ASSUME Y quantised; and the conditions are HOMOGENEOUS so they can NEVER fix Y's normalisation, only ratios. B950's ledger line that the hypercharges are the SM's only computed value-level structure STANDS BUT MUST BE QUALIFIED: forced up to normalisation, per generation, and given assumptions the object may not supply. (5) Q3 -- IT HAS BEEN DONE, AND CLOSE TO HOME: Todorov, JHEP 04 (2021) 164, 'Superselection of the weak hypercharge', states verbatim that Y is promoted to a superselection rule commuting with all observables and that THE CENTRALIZER OF Y IN so(10) IS u(2)+u(3) -- i.e. su(3)+su(2)+u(1)+u(1), the SM algebra plus one extra abelian factor, FROM A CENTRALIZER CONSTRUCTION: structurally L132's own move, one u(1) short, in so(10) rather than e6. Krasnov 2021 gives a commutant characterisation of all of G_SM, and Todorov-Dubois-Violette derive the SM symmetry from J3(O) via Borel-de Siebenthal -- while this programme's own build IS M(O,C) (P70/B904). THE OCTONIONIC-JORDAN ROUTE TO THE SM IS OCCUPIED LITERATURE. (6) WHAT L132 COULD HONESTLY CLAIM IF RUN: only a STATED-IN-ADVANCE principle selecting which u(1) is hypercharge from the object's own measurement structure -- meaningful only if fixed BEFORE looking at which combination gives the right answer, else postdiction -- and, if the spectrum does NOT form complete 27s, the anomaly constraint becomes genuine. Everything else is REPRODUCED, never predicted. Named traps: do not claim Y's normalisation; do not claim 'hypercharge falls out' if an SU(5)/SO(10) subgroup was chosen, INCLUDING IMPLICITLY BY READING STANDARD BRANCHING TABLES since that choice IS the identification; do not treat commutant-derivation-of-Y as a novel genre. (7) THE PANEL'S HONESTY CAVEAT, CARRIED: control PASSED before any null was trusted (Geng-Marshak PRD 39 (1989) 693 with all 170 citing works enumerated; the E6 vocabulary surfaced by citation weight); INSPIRE-HEP, arXiv, ar5iv, OpenAlex and zbMATH reached; MATHSCINET NOT REACHED (302 auth wall) and no claim rests on it; and THE Q3 NULL IS NOT CERTIFIED -- the octonion/Jordan literature is large, fast-moving and partly outside INSPIRE's core indexing, so it reads as 'not found by this sweep', never 'does not exist'.
